static_traits.name: Ma Xiu
static_traits.family_status: Having two nephews; the older brother serves in the military
static_traits.social_status: Work performance is affected; prioritizing running slightly affects relationships with family; has support from an elder brother and several friends, but has not yet discussed these feelings with them in detail
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not experienced similar psychological problems in the past, has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and fairly coherently; cooperative with a positive attitude; able to describe triggering situations and emotional changes concretely

basic_info.main_problem: I feel that if I cannot go running, my whole week is ruined, which triggers anxiety and disappointment.
basic_info.core_demands: I am willing to look for other coping methods, so that when I cannot run I will not be so anxious.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, because work was exceptionally busy and the client could not schedule runs, the client began to form a chain of worries that 'missing one run will lead to losing control and the whole week being ruined'; afterward, whenever the client missed a run due to an unpredictable work schedule, the client would feel strong anxiety and loss of control, affecting concentration, sleep, and eating; the client has long relied on running as the main way to relieve stress and lacks other alternative strategies.

core_beliefs: My mind-body balance and control depend entirely on whether I run
As long as I miss one run, this week will become bad or be ruined

special_situations.event: Work is unusually busy or schedule is unpredictable, causing inability to run that day
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I miss one run, I will lose control over my body and mind, and the whole week will fall apart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Rigidly schedules running as the top priority, trying to make other matters give way to running
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This week is ruined; I cannot hold on under the work pressure.

special_situations.event: Social activities conflict with the scheduled running time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not put running first, my condition will worsen and affect work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding or reducing social activities to ensure being able to run
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Going will disrupt the rhythm, and everything will be worse afterward.

special_situations.event: Noticing a day in the weekly plan when running cannot be scheduled
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One gap means failure for the whole week
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping oneself busier to withstand the anxiety, trying to 'tough it out'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as I did not run today, I will keep missing runs afterward.

special_situations.event: Recalls past experiences of occasionally missing a run (the week was not entirely bad), yet focuses only on the negative experience
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only fully adhering to the plan counts as good, a little deviation is a bad week
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ruminating on negative outcomes, ignoring positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always handle things badly; one mistake and everything is wrong.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to maintain self-control and mind-body balance through regular running
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control, being overwhelmed by anxiety and causing impaired work performance
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of safety and stability by rigidly persisting in running and prioritizing it

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable individual who needs to rely on running to maintain balance
object_relations.object_representation: An unpredictable external environment and others' arrangements that disrupt one's rhythm

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When work or social activities invited by others affect the established running schedule
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Unconsciously experiences external demands as a threat to self-balance, believing that without running things will spiral out of control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a firm but polite tone, emphasizes that running must be adhered to, listing in detail reasons for not participating in social activities or adjusting arrangements to prove its 'rationality'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When realizing that running is impossible on a certain day, or when invited in counseling to explore coping strategies other than running
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets 'missing one run' as the whole week being ruined (transference into strong anxiety about control)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses absolute and 'all-or-nothing' wording (such as 'it is over' and 'all ruined'), with a tense, conclusive tone, weakening discussion of grays and possibilities.

manifestations: A strong need to maintain a sense of control over life through a fixed running routine
Feeling one's autonomy is restricted when facing unpredictable work schedules
Sacrificing socializing to maintain the pace
outcomes: Significant anxiety and loss of control
Sleep and eating routines are affected

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Common language includes 'I must / should...' and 'everyone is like this'.
manifestations: Using 'must keep running' as a rigid standard to maintain stability
Viewing schedule and performance with 'should' 'must' self-demands
Treats the fixed rhythm as the only correct choice, ignoring other possible coping methods

exception_events.target_problem: When missing a run, the client usually experiences strong anxiety, finds it hard to focus, and worries the whole week will be 'ruined'.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a few occasions when the client missed runs due to busy work, although still anxious, the client kept themselves busier and 'pushed through', the week was not completely terrible, and work was able to proceed.
exception_events.reason: Different context and approach: the work tasks were more saturated at the time, creating distraction; the client adopted a strategy of staying highly engaged and busy, thereby partially relieving the worry that 'the whole week will be ruined'.

positive_force: Willing to explore alternative coping strategies besides running
Has a habit of persisting with self-management (running as a stabilizer)
Maintains contact with older brother and friends; has some social support
Positive attitude toward counseling, willing to practice de-catastrophizing
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white cognition lead to escalating anxiety
Excessive reliance on a single coping method (only running to relieve stress)
Mental filtering and overgeneralization cause positive evidence to be ignored
An unpredictable work schedule increases trigger frequency and feelings of losing control

target_behavior.behavior: When missing one run, strong anxiety and a sense of losing control appear, reacting with the absolute cognition that 'the whole week is ruined'
antecedent: Unpredictable or unusually busy work schedule causes inability to run as planned
Social activities conflict with running time
Seeing a day in the weekly plan when running cannot be scheduled
target_behavior.core_reason: Long regards running as the only effective way to relieve stress and maintain control; holds catastrophizing, all-or-nothing, and overgeneralizing cognitions about missing a run, worrying about continued loss of control afterward.
target_behavior.function: Escapes unwelcome anxious experiences and quickly restores a subjective sense of control (through a rigid schedule and prioritizing running); avoids socializing to reduce the risk of the rhythm being disrupted.
target_behavior.consequence: Work focus declined, sleep and eating affected; socializing reduced and interaction with family impaired, overall quality of life lowered.
